En septembre 2026, l&#39;inflation accél: In September 2026, inflation picked up, driven by energy. In the United States, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.6% year on year, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis (29 October). In the euro area, the harmonised index rose 3.8%, with energy up 18.9%, according to Eurostat (16 October). In Japan, the national index rose 2.1%, according to the Statistics Bureau (23 October). All three central banks aim for 2%. But that figure does not mean the same thing at the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of Japan (BoJ): coverage, the weight of housing and formulas differ. This article explains how to read these indices, where inflation comes from, why it persists and why Japan faces the opposite problem.

La Fed vise 2 % sur le PCE, calculé par: The Fed targets 2% as measured by the PCE, calculated by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) (22 August 2025 strategy). The ECB targets 2%, symmetrically and over the medium term, as measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) (30 June 2025 strategy). The BoJ targets 2% as measured by the national consumer price index (CPI) (22 January 2013 target). The table compares the three indices on what makes their figures diverge.
Inclut les dépenses payées par des tiers: Includes expenditure paid by third parties (health)
Le logement des propriétaires est la dif: Owner-occupied housing is the biggest difference (methods: BEA, Eurostat, Statistics Bureau; figures published on 29, 16 and 23 October). In December 2025, housing accounted for 35.6% of the US CPI, including 26.2% for owners' equivalent rent (BLS). The ECB tracks it separately.
PCE contre CPI, IPC contre IPCH: PCE versus CPI, French CPI versus HICP
Le BEA décompose l&#39;écart entre son i: The BEA breaks down the gap between its index and the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) CPI into formula, weight and scope effects, plus a residual (FAQ 555). Over 2002–2007, the CPI rose by about 0.4 percentage point a year more than the PCE: the formula explained about half of the gap, the weight of housing the rest, with health care working in the opposite direction (McCully, Moyer and Stewart, 2007). This is one of the reasons put forward for targeting the PCE, which is considered more comprehensive.
En 2026, l&#39;écart s&#39;est inversé s: In 2026, the gap reversed for core inflation, excluding food and energy: 3.0% for the PCE against 2.4% for the CPI in August (BEA, BLS), then 3.1% against 2.6% in September (BEA, BLS). As the BEA's reconciliation table could not be found on 8 October, the explanation remains an interpretation. By deduction, housing is not the cause: it rose 3.0% in the CPI in August, more than core, and weighs less in the PCE. A note from an asset manager points to items that the CPI ignores or weights lightly, which have risen sharply since January: software, portfolio management, legal services (ANIMA, 28 August 2026, unquantified commentary). Yet the price of portfolio management follows the stock market, not pressure on consumer prices.
En France, l&#39;IPC progresse de 3,0 %: In France, the consumer price index (INSEE's IPC) rose 3.0% and the HICP 3.4% in September 2026, according to the provisional estimate (INSEE, 30 Sept.). The HICP measures health net of reimbursements, includes non-market education and health and, since 2026, gambling (methodological note); the share of each item has not been established. Only the HICP is used to assess the ECB's target.
L&#39;inflation sous-jacente retire les: Core inflation removes volatile items, but not the same ones everywhere: food and energy in the United States; energy, food, alcohol and tobacco in the euro area. In Japan, the widely cited “core” removes only fresh food and keeps energy; the “core-core” removes both. In August 2026, the first stood at 1.7%, the second at 1.9% (Statistics Bureau, 18 Sept.).
D&#39;autres mesures écartent chaque moi: Other measures strip out extreme changes each month: the trimmed mean PCE of the Dallas Fed, the median CPI of the Cleveland Fed. In August, they stood between 2.2% and 2.6%, a sign that the rise was concentrated in a few items. In the euro area, the range of measures tracked by the ECB ran from 2.9% to 6.9% in June 2023 (Bańbura et al., 2023). None dominates in all circumstances, and removing energy can mask its spread to other prices when the shock lasts.
Chaque chiffre a enfin plusieurs vies. L: Finally, each figure has several lives. The HICP first appears as a flash estimate at the end of the month, then as final data around the middle of the following month: September energy went from 18.8% (2 Oct.) to 18.9% (16 Oct.). The unadjusted CPI is final on publication, but its seasonally adjusted version is revised back five years every February (BLS).
Outil : glissement annuel, rythme annual: Tool: year-on-year rate, annualised rate, base effect
Le glissement annuel compare un mois au: The year-on-year rate compares a month with the same month of the previous year. The annualised rate scales a short-period change up to a full year; it requires a seasonally adjusted series.
Avec l&#39;indice des prix PCE (millésim: Using the PCE price index (vintage of 30 September 2026, FRED, extracted on 7 October), the calculation gives, for August 2026, 3.42% year on year (131.579 / 127.229 − 1), 3.57% at an annualised rate over six months and 1.03% over three months, dragged down by a fall in the index in June.
L&#39;effet de base : en septembre 2025,: The base effect: in September 2025, the index had risen by 0.29%. With that month dropping out of the calculation, a 0.2% rise in September 2026 would have brought the year-on-year rate down to 3.32%, without any fall in prices. The BEA ultimately published 3.6% on 29 October.
Les millésimes, c&#39;est-à-dire l&#39;é: Vintages, that is, the state of a series at a given publication date: the annual update of the accounts on 30 September 2026 revised the index back to January 2021 (BEA). The June-to-July rise, annualised, falls from 1.89% to 0.61% depending on the vintage; mixing the two produces a fictitious fall. The attribution of the earlier levels to the 26 August vintage is inferred from the ALFRED page, not verified by download.
<span class=\"n\">02</span>Un choc d&#39: 02An energy shock only becomes lasting through second-round effects
La plupart des travaux récents partent d: Most recent work starts from the expectations-augmented Phillips curve: inflation equals expected inflation, plus an effect of labour market tightness, plus cost shocks. The slope of the curve measures how sensitive inflation is to this tightness, judged by the gap between unemployment and its equilibrium level, which is estimated, not observed. Excess demand, supply shocks and margins only make inflation last if they pass through to wages and expectations.

Energy shock

  → persistent inflation
Tant que le choc reste un prix relatif,: As long as the shock remains a relative price, its effect on inflation fades. Faced with a supply shock, a rate hike does not target the price of energy, but second-round effects.
Le CPI américain a culminé à 9,1 % sur u: The US CPI peaked at 9.1% year on year in June 2022, in unadjusted data (BLS, 13 July 2022). The HICP peaked at 10.6% in October 2022 (10.7% in the flash estimate; Eurostat, 17 November 2022). Three readings, more complementary than mutually exclusive, dominate.
Pour <a href=\"https://doi.org/10.1257/m: For Bernanke and Blanchard (2025), a peer-reviewed article, the US rise came mainly from shocks to energy, food and shortages; labour market tightness weighed less at the time, but lasted longer. Their working paper on eleven economies (2024) adds that the shocks did not become entrenched, partly thanks to credible targets. Ball, Leigh and Mishra (2022, Brookings Papers) emphasise the pass-through of shocks to core inflation, which also reflects the tightness measured by the ratio of job vacancies to unemployed workers. For the euro area, Hansen, Toscani and Zhou (2023), in a working paper that does not represent the views of the IMF, attribute about 40% of the rise in the consumption deflator between the first quarters of 2022 and 2023 to import prices, and 45% to domestic profits, without a generalised rise in margins.
Ces estimations de modèle ne tranchent n: These model estimates settle neither the role of fiscal policy nor the question of a reaction that came too late, argued by Reis (2022) in a Bank for International Settlements working paper that reflects only his own views: in his account, central banks underestimated the risk of de-anchoring.
<a href=\"https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qj: Hazell, Herreño, Nakamura and Steinsson (2022) estimate a flat slope using US state data: reducing inflation through slower activity alone is costly in unemployment, and the disinflation of the 1980s would have been driven mainly by expectations. Benigno and Eggertsson, in a working paper not published in a journal, argue that the slope steepens when the labour market is very tight, which would explain the rapid rise of 2021–2022 and then disinflation without recession; the hypothesis remains debated. Finally, firms' expectations, studied in New Zealand, are dispersed and poorly informed (Coibion, Gorodnichenko and Kumar, 2018).
Dans un exemple aux valeurs d&#39;école: In an example with textbook values (expectations at 2.5%, a slope of 0.2, unemployment half a percentage point below equilibrium), bringing inflation down from 2.6% to 2% with unchanged expectations would require 3 percentage points more unemployment; if expectations return to 2%, it is enough for unemployment to return to its equilibrium level. With a flat slope, credibility does most of the work: a credible central bank can look through a supply shock, one that is not must react more strongly. Any estimated slope remains very imprecise (Mavroeidis, Plagborg-Møller and Stock, 2014).

Le premier tour domine en Europe ; aux É: The first round dominates in Europe; in the United States, core inflation shows that the problem is not just energy (sources: Eurostat, BEA, BLS, Statistics Bureau). In the euro area, headline inflation exceeds inflation excluding energy by 1.5 percentage points (calculation: 3.8 − 2.3); AFP links the shock to the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East in early July (3 Oct. 2026, press, causality not established). The rise in services inflation, from 3.0% in August to 3.2% in September (flash estimate), may still reflect indirect effects, and no published decomposition covers this shock. <span class=\"n\">03</span>Le Japon a lo: 03Japan has long fought the opposite problem
De la fin des années 1990 au début des a: From the late 1990s to the early 2010s, Japan experienced deflation or inflation close to zero. The mechanism is persistence in reverse: expectations anchored near zero and sluggish wages hold back any pick-up. According to a BoJ working paper that does not represent the views of the institution, the zero lower bound on interest rates and subdued expectations prevented 2% from being reached on a lasting basis, and the price–wage cycle strengthened after the pandemic (Fukunaga, Hogen and Ueno, 2024).
Après l&#39;adoption de la cible de 2 %: After the adoption of the 2% target in January 2013, quantitative and qualitative easing (April 2013), the negative interest rate (January 2016) and yield curve control (September 2016) were aimed at shifting these expectations. According to De Michelis and Iacoviello (2016), raising a target has limited effects when its credibility is low. Using its own model, the BoJ estimates the effect of these policies at 0.5–0.7 percentage point of inflation (December 2024 review). These measures ended on 19 March 2024 (BoJ).
En 2026, le débat porte sur la mesure. L: In 2026, the debate is about measurement. On 18 September, the BoJ wrote that underlying inflation “has been approaching 2 percent” (statement); its two dissenters were looking at the index excluding fresh food, still at 1.7% in August. In September, the headline index (2.1%) remained below the measure excluding fresh food and energy (2.4%): taken together, these two items are rising less than the rest. On 30 October, the Outlook report judged underlying inflation “broadly consistent” with 2% and projected, as the median of Policy Board members, 2.5%, 2.6% and then 2.0% excluding fresh food for fiscal years 2026 to 2028 (Outlook); one member, Hajime Takata, considered the target already achieved (statement). In Japan, the question is no longer how to exit deflation, but whether inflation close to 2% is becoming embedded in wages.
L&#39;inversion de l&#39;écart sous-jace: The reversal of the core gap between the PCE and the CPI remains unexplained until the BEA's reconciliation table has been read. The financial-items lead rests on unquantified commentary, which itself expects the gap to narrow after methodological revisions.
